statement: d06 started with coordination hub down: both ocentra_enforcer_coordination_claim and ocentra_enforcer_coordination_mail MCP tools returned {ok:false, error:'MCP server is stale; refusing ... because it may write incompatible coordination events', reloadRequired:true} at session start, matching the persistent hub-down condition e01 logged earlier in this build. Per protocol (log+proceed), d06 proceeded without a ledger claim or a 'd06 started' mail and built its owned files directly.
why: Confirms the hub-down condition spans multiple lanes/sessions in this build window, not a one-off; an orchestrator or hub-repair task should not treat absent d06 ledger events as evidence the work did not happen.
howToApply: Check git log on lane/d06 directly rather than the coordination ledger for d06's claim/lifecycle history.

statement: d06's own two named upstream deps for the fix/review phases -- d07 (enforcer-coordination self-correct fix loop) and d10 (resilience-auditor obligation rows) -- have NOT landed a Rust API on rust-build as of this build. enforcer-coordination::api.rs exposes only hub/lane/claim/guard/ledger/presence/sync (no fix-loop entry point at all); there is no auditor crate or module anywhere in the workspace. Rather than block or fake these two phases, fix_oracle() fails closed with an explicit FailReason::NotYetWired (same posture enforcer-cli::commands/main.rs already uses for install/plan/proof/coordination before their owning workpacks land), and review_oracle() wires ONLY the half that HAS landed (enforcer-proof::claim's pr_ready gate) while explicitly not consulting the d10 evidence it cannot yet check.
why: The workpack's own acceptance bar is fail-closed ('no phase can report success unless its oracle returns a pass'); silently no-op-passing fix/review's auditor half, or inventing a placeholder oracle that always passes, would violate that bar more severely than an honest NotYetWired failure does.
howToApply: When d07 lands a fix-loop entry point in enforcer-coordination, replace fix_oracle()'s body with a real delegation call (same shape as check_oracle -> enforcer_scan::engine) and add its own fail/pass fixture-tree tests to tests/lifecycle.rs. When d10 lands an auditor crate/module, extend review_oracle to also gate on its obligation rows.

statement: The workspace's clippy deny wall (unwrap_used/expect_used = deny in the root Cargo.toml [lints]) applies to test files (tests/*.rs), not just src/*.rs -- cargo clippy -p enforcer-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings failed on tests/lifecycle.rs's std::env::current_dir().expect(...)/Mutex::lock().expect(...) calls even though they were only in a #[cfg(test)]-free integration test binary. Converting them to `?`-propagated Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> test fns (the same pattern every other #[test] fn in this crate already uses) satisfied the lint; a bare .map_err(|_| "...") also tripped clippy::map_err_ignore (deny) and had to become .map_err(|poisoned| format!("...: {poisoned}")) to keep the source error visible.
why: A worker assuming test code is exempt from the crate's own lint deny wall will get a clippy failure that looks like a src/ bug but is actually in tests/, and the map_err_ignore trap compounds it if they reach for the obvious `.map_err(|_| ...)` fix.
howToApply: In this workspace, write every #[test] fn as -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> and use `?` instead of .unwrap()/.expect() from the start, including in tests/*.rs integration files, not just src/*.rs; never `.map_err(|_| ...)`, always bind and use the original error.
